                         GAINER FAMILY’S REPLY BRIEF

       COME NOW, Franklin and Jane Gainer, Sally Guitar, and Matthew and Mindy

Gainer (collectively, the “Gainer Family”) and file this Reply Brief in the above-captioned

proceeding in accordance with 16 Texas Administrative Code (“TAC”) § 22.124. The Gainer

Family respectfully show as follows:

                                       INTRODUCTION

       The Gainer Family, through this Reply Brief, advocates for the proposal and adoption of

Route 894 as the “best meets” route in this proceeding, and against the selection of Routes 572,

CCG, and 295/296 as the “best meets” route. In that regard, the Gainer Family adopts and

incorporates by reference here Sections I and II of the Reply Brief filed by the G6 Landowners

Legal Fund, LLC (Party 324) with respect to Routes 894, 572, CCG, and 295/296.




                                                   1
         The Gainer Family is also opposed to the adoption of Route 487 as the “best meets” route,

This Reply Brief is directed at responding to issues and arguments regarding that route. The Gainer

Family respectfully suggests that the Administrative Law Judges (the “ALJs”) consider reviewing

the Reply Brief filed by the G6 Landowners Legal Fund, LLC in advance of and in conjunction

with their review of this Reply Brief.

        The evidentiary record demonstrates that Route 894, as proposed by the Applicants, best

complies with the statutory and regulatory factors that govern this proceeding and should be

recommended by the ALJs and adopted by the Commission. The Gainer Family respectfully

requests that the ALJs propose, and the Commission adopt Route 894 as the “best meets” route for

this proceeding.

        The Gainer Family shows as follows:

                            I. ROUTE 487 IS INFERIOR TO ROUTE 894

        The briefing filed in this matter has not changed the fundamental facts demonstrating that

Route 487 is inferior to Route 894. The Applicants recommended filing 122 of the 1,246

alternative routes with the Application for the Commission’s consideration. Through further

analysis, the Applicants identified a Top 6 list of routes, which included Routes 469, 488, 509,

894, and 902.1 Route 487 did not make the cut, and for good reason.

        Route 487 has 96 habitable structures within 500 feet of its centerline.2 Eleven more

habitable structures will be impacted by Route 487 than Route 894, which impacts only 85

habitable structures, the third fewest of all routes proposed by the Applicants.




1
 Party 641, Link N3 Opposition, N3 Exhibit 12 Native File.
2
 Application, Attachment l at Table 7-2; see also PUC Staff Ex.1, Attachments JP-5 and JP-7; Poole Direct
Testimony, Interchange Filing No. 5029, at 60:9-61.

                                                        2
         Route 487 relies on the J11 Link, which runs within 100 feet of the north boundary of the

park. Mr. Poole acknowledged that Colorado Bend State Park is 100 feet from the J11 Link. 3 Brady

Creek/Wulff Ranch (Party 574) provided a stark and graphic depiction of the impact Route 487

would have on the public’s access to and enjoyment of the Colorado Bend State Park. 4 Mr. Poole

agreed that standing on the west bank of the river, Route 487 would run directly in front of the

Park fencing.5 The proximity of Route 487 to this state park eliminates it as an appropriate

selection as the “best meets” route.

        Mr. Poole agreed that apparent property boundary measures are less reliable than existing

compatible infrastructure measures.6 He referred to it as “an imperfect metric.” 7 The ALJs’

recommendation should not be based on an imperfect metric, particularly given the fact that Route

487 impacts more habitable structures than does Route 894 and crosses directly in front of the

fenceline for Colorado Bend State Park.

        Route 487 performs particularly poorly on other environmental factors. Route 487 crosses

271,429 feet of riparian areas, performing 127th of the 132 routes Mr. Poole reviewed.8 Route 487

crosses potential wetlands for 11,471 feet of its length, ranking 105th of the 132 routes Mr. Poole

reviewed.9

        The Gainers are not alone in concluding that Route 487 is inferior to Route 894. Lampasas

J11 Landowners (Party 503), noted the following:




3
  Poole Direct Testimony, Interchange Filing No. 5029, at 40:18.
4
  Party 574, Brady Creek/Wulff Bluff Exhibit 59; see also Poole, Transcript, Vol. IV, 174:23-175:15.
5
  Poole, Transcript, Vol. IV, 175:12-18.
6
  Id., at 172:8-10.
7
  Id., at 172:12-15.
8
  Poole Direct Testimony, Interchange No. 5029, at 45:13-14.
9
  Id., at 45:16–18.

                                                         3
             •   Any construction along the J11 Link would disturb Indian burial grounds, an
                existing navigable water way, federal wetlands, and further endanger existing
                endangered species.10
            •   The proposed route is in extreme proximity to the regulated floodplain protected by
                an adjoining flood-control dam (Soil Conservation Service Site 6) which is
                immediately on the same property. The dam is over 70 years old and was originally
                constructed with a 50-year life span. If the J11 Link is used, further destabilization
                of the dam structure itself and similar infrastructure in the vicinity could create a
                catastrophic flood risk that could not only endanger but take the lives of any
                unfortunate people downstream.11

        Cherokee Creek witness, Ms. Reinecke, noted that the J11 Link is one of the links which

crosses the Colorado River at a Texas Parks & Wildlife Department-designated Ecologically

Significant Stream Segment. 12

        CE Stephens observed, “[E]very route (including Routes 487, 572, and CCG) that uses

Link N4 impact a greater number of habitable structures than the routes that do not use Link N4.” 13

        Link N3 Opposition Landowners contend that the N3 Link (which Route 894 uses but

Route 487 does not) should not be used simply based on the number of landowners along the N3

Link that have intervened. There is no basis under the applicable statute or rules for a routing

decision to be made on such a consideration. The outcome of this proceeding cannot be determined

by an “unpopularity” contest, but rather should be based on an independent, unbiased review of

the potential routes and how they match up against the required statutory and regulatory factors.



10
   Party 503, Lampasas J11 Landowners Exhibit 3, Direct Testimony of Antal Pataky at 4; Lampasas J11
Landowners Exhibit 1, Direct Testimony of Todd Lively at 4; Lampasas J11 Landowners Exhibit 2, Direct
Testimony of Stephen Ellison at 4.
11
   Party 503, Lampasas J11 Landowners Direct Testimony of Todd Lively at 4-5; Lampasas J11 Landowners Exhibit
2, Direct Testimony of Stephen Ellison at 4-5.
12
   Party 474, CCP Exhibit 1, Reinecke Direct Testimony, Interchange Filing No. 4204, at 42-43.
13
   Party 642, CE Stephens Initial Brief, Interchange Filing No. 6251, at 16.

                                                      4
 No party wants the route to affect its property. It has been appropriately noted, however, “A

landowner not wanting the line on or near their property is not a differentiating factor in selecting

a route for the line.” 14 The selection of any of the proposed routes will take a toll on the

communities affected. These facts mandate a thorough review of all the factors.

        And the Gainer Family would be dramatically impacted by use of the N4 Link. As CE

Stephens observed in its Initial Brief:

            The problem of fragmentation caused by Link N4 and the routes that use N4 is not
            isolated to Sola Fe Ranch. Link N4 also splits a ranch, owned by the Gainer Family,
            identified as Property ID Nos. 451, 452, 453, 454, 456, 457, and 458. As Ms. Magers'
            points out, the fragmentation of these two properties was quickly identified using
            publicly available data; therefore, there is a likelihood of there being more similar
            ranches on Link N4 that are not properly identified as contiguous single
            properties. 15

These incidents of fragmentation are expected to occur across the scope of the Project, whatever

route is selected. This fact emphasizes the importance of relying on an independent, unbiased

analysis of all of the routing possibilities. Only one party has conducted such a review – the

Applicants – and the Applicants determined that Route 894 was the “best meets” route. Under this

independent analysis, Route 487 did not even make it to the Top 6 of potential routes.

        Link N3 Opposition Landowners also urge the ALJs and the Commission to engage in a

link-based cost analysis as opposed to a route-based analysis but provide no basis or support for

the propriety of such an analysis. As the ALJs and the Commission are aware, the routing decision

is to be determined at the route level.




14
  Party 40, Theon-Voss Initial Brief, Interchange Filing No. 6259, at 4.
15
  Party 642, CE Stephens; Initial Brief, Interchange Filing No. 6251, at 12, citing CE Stephens Exh. 2 - Magers
Cross Reb. at 3.

          Link N3 Opposition Landowners concludes its Initial Brief with the following

recommendation, “Overall, the Commission should select a route that uses N4 or N12 instead of

N3, including Route 296, as the route that best meets the routing criteria in PURA § 37.056 and

16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B).” As noted in the G6 Landowners Legal Fund, LLC’s Reply Brief,

adopted here with respect to Route 296, among others, Route 296 is disfavored for several reasons,

including:

             •   Route 296 did not make Applicants’ list of the Top 6 routes, 16 even before the
                 Applicants became aware of the existence and location of the Florence Elementary
                 School;
             •   The location of Route 296 immediately adjacent to the Florence Elementary School
                 is a fatal flaw for that route and would have negatively impacted both the
                 Applicants’ and the PUC staff’s evaluation of Route 296 if they had been aware of
                 the presence of the school;17
             •   Route 894 clearly outperforms Route 296 when considering historical values; 18
             •   Route 296’s use of the G31 Link presents a significant engineering constraint due
                 to pipeline rights-of-way affecting the path;19
             •   Route 296 utilizes the J31 Link, which appears to cross directly though land
                 designated as Golden-Cheeked Warbler (“GCW”) mitigation acreage; 20
             •   Mr. Poole agreed the J31 Link was “problematic” 21 and further agreed that this
                 crossing would be “another reason [why] 29622 is not the appropriate route” for this
                 project;23 and

19
   Party 357, Direct Testimony, Exh_001, Interchange Filing No. 4071, at 4.

analysis.

                                                          6
                •   Route 894 is superior to Routes 295 and 296 in several routing categories, perhaps
                   most significantly, length; cost; and habitable structures.

           The Gainer Family respectfully requests that Link N3 Opposition Landowners’ arguments

and recommendation be rejected as contrary to the record and that the ALJs propose, and the

Commission adopt Route 894 as the “best meets” route for this proceeding.


                             II. CONCLUSION AND REQUESTED RELIEF

           Oncor Engineer Casey Petty accurately stated, “Much of the opposition to Route 894

focuses on issues like impacts to recreational enjoyment, wildlife, and hunting land; impacts to

cattle grazing and livestock operations; aesthetic and visual impacts; historical and cultural

resources impacts related to Native American artifacts; among similar issues. Each of these

criticisms concern constraints or community values that would be present at some point along

every alternative route.”24

           This Reply Brief has adopted the briefing filed by the G6 Landowners Legal Fund, LLC

supporting the selection of Route 894. As discussed in greater detail there, the Applicants

conducted an in-depth and unbiased review of data and public input, captured in a 2,800-page

report. They analyzed thousands of route permutations, narrowing these first to 1,246 alternative

routes, then to 122 routes filed with the Application, then to a list of the Top 30 routes, and

ultimately to a list of the Top 6 routes.

           Through this process, the Applicants have determined that Route 894 is the “best meets”

route for this proceeding. The majority of experts who have testified in this matter, who have




24
     Applicant, Petty Cross-Rebuttal Testimony, Interchange Filing No. 5212, at 4:18-23.

                                                           7
 reviewed and analyzed the available information from different perspectives using different

approaches, have also confirmed that Route 894 is the “best meets” route.

       Parties whose properties lie along the path of Route 894 have, unsurprisingly, proposed

other routes that will avoid impacts to their properties and interests. This Reply Brief has also

adopted the briefing filed by the G6 Landowners Legal Fund, LLC where it addressed arguments

made in support of Routes 572, CCG, 296 and 295.

       The Gainer Family has also demonstrated above that Route 487 is inferior to Route 894

and should be rejected from consideration as the “best meets” route for this proceeding.

       The Gainer Family appreciates the consideration of these issues and respectfully requests

that the Administrative Law Judges propose, and the Commission adopt Route 894 as the “best

meets” route for this proceeding.

       If Route 894 is not selected as the “best meets” route, the Gainer Family would support the

selection of an alternative route utilizing Link N12 through Concho County, Texas. Specifically,

they support the selection of Route Nos. 392 and 410 if Route 894 is not selected as the “best

meets” route.

       In addition, if Route 894 is not selected as the “best meets” route, the Gainer Family

supports the RFI route proposed by Link R1 Opposition Landowners, designated as “Route 894

Western Mod 1.”
